order.why_here: The first primitive: flip arrows one at a time with prev/cur/nxt, saving next before each rewire.
The second primitive: a dummy head and a tail pointer that splices existing nodes into an output chain.
Same dummy-and-tail splice, but the output nodes are new and a carry rides along the lockstep walk.
Two runners with a fixed gap measure distance from the end in one pass; the dummy makes deleting the head ordinary.
Two runners at different speeds: on a loop the gap shrinks by one per tick, so fast must meet slow.
Turns the meeting point into a ruler: walking from head and from the meeting point at equal speed lands on the loop entrance.
An array whose values are indices is a hidden linked list, so the same two-phase Floyd finds the repeated value.
Equalise the remaining lengths, then walk in lockstep; the gap idea used to align two lists instead of one.
First combination of primitives: find the middle, reverse the back half, compare the halves.
All three primitives together: find the middle, reverse the back half, splice the halves alternately.
Adds an old-to-new node mapping, then removes the hash map by weaving each clone right after its original.
The capstone: reversal bounded to blocks of k, with look-ahead and careful reconnection of every block.
